subject: Follow-up: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens for Acme pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens for Acme pilot

Hi Samantha 

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so our pricing model matches Acme's expected economics:

Recap (from our discovery):
- Expected pilot monthly volume: ~100M user tokens (with peak days up to ~200M).
- Main workload: customer support assistant + product search re-ranking. High prompt reuse across sessions (repeated prefixes: system + product taxonomy).
- Target monthly spend range you mentioned: $10k$15k for pilot (goal is to validate ROI before expanding).
- Procurement will need SOW + pricing workbook for review.

Key pricing questions we promised to validate:
1) Which effective $/1M tokens would you target for the pilot to be viable? (you mentioned ~$10$15/1M as a target on the call)
2) Rough cache hit expectations for prefix reuse (how often do prompts contain identical system+context prefixes?).

Our initial assumptions we used to build the attached pricing_model.xlsx:
- Retail list price (baseline, no caching): $25.00 / 1M tokens billed.
- Prefix cache assumptions: if Acme can reuse prefixes across sessions (e.g., same system prompt + product taxonomy chunk), we typically see 4070% prefix cache hit in similar customers depending on session patterns.
- Simple effective cost calc: effective $/1M user tokens = list_price * (1 - cache_hit_rate). Example: $25 * (1 - 0.60) = $10 / 1M user tokens.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the pilot target effective $/1M you need (confirm $10$15/1M)?
- Can you share any telemetry (sample of prompt shapes or percent of sessions with identical prefixes) or a short example of the typical prompt+response so we can sanity-check the hit-rate assumption?
- I'll send a follow-up with a couple pricing scenarios (baseline, 40% cache, 60% cache) and a recommended pilot commitment that matches your budget range.

Attaching the pricing_model we discussed and a draft SOW for procurement.

Thanks  talk soon,
Marissa

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from our side: 

1) Pilot target economics: we’d ideally like to see effective pricing in the $8$12 / 1M tokens range to make the business case for production. If caching gets us to ~$8/1M, that would be great.

2) Volumes: our conservative estimate for the pilot is 80150M user tokens / month (average ~100M). Peak days could approach 200M.

3) Cache-hit signals: a lot of our workflows reuse the same system prompt + product taxonomy block. We don’t have exact hit-rate telemetry yet but think 50>60% prefix reuse is plausible for the assistant flows; search re-ranking is lower (maybe 2040% reuse). We can extract sample prompt hashes for you next week.

Great  appreciate the quick answers, Samantha. Attached is an updated pricing summary (pricing_model.xlsx) with three scenarios and the assumptions baked in. I'll paste the short, plain-English math below so procurement can follow.

Assumptions used in the workbook:
- List price (no caching): $25.00 / 1M billed tokens.
- Cache hit types: prefix cache (reused prompt prefixes across sessions) and KV cache (session-level). For pilot economics we focused on prefix cache only since your reuse happens across users/sessions.
- Example workload breakdown (pilot average): 70% assistant flows (high prefix reuse), 30% re-rank/search (low reuse).

Scenario math (high-level):
- Scenario A: No cache
  - Effective $/1M user tokens = $25.00
- Scenario B: 40% prefix cache hit (conservative for assistant flows)
  - Effective $/1M user tokens = $25 * (1 - 0.40) = $15.00
- Scenario C: 60% prefix cache hit (achievable if prompts are highly reused)
  - Effective $/1M user tokens = $25 * (1 - 0.60) = $10.00

Applying to your pilot numbers (example at 100M user tokens / month):
- No cache: cost = 100 * $25 = $2,500 (this is billed in units of 1M tokens => $25 * 100 = $2,500) 
- 40% cache: cost = 100 * $15 = $1,500
- 60% cache: cost = 100 * $10 = $1,000

Notes on the calc: the workbook models token billing on the billed tokens after cache (billed_tokens = total_user_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate)); the effective $/1M shown in the workbook is the normalized $ per 1M of user tokens (list_price * (1 - hit_rate)).

Recommendations / next steps:
1) If Acme can confirm a 5060% effective prefix hit for assistant flows we can match your $8$12/1M target by combining pilot commitment and the cache uplift. For example, if blended pilot hit ends up ~60% we land at ~$10/1M which aligns with your stated target.
2) Share a small sample (anonymized) of prompt shapes or prompt-hash distribution and we will run a quick estimate to validate the 5060% hit assumption.
3) If procurement needs tighter unit economics we can propose a pilot commitment (3 months / minimum monthly commitment) with tiered pricing tied to measured cache hit after month 1.

Attaching: pricing_model.xlsx (detailed scenarios) and draft Acme_SOW_v1.pdf.

If that all sounds reasonable I’ll schedule a quick 20-min call with your engineering lead next week to get the prompt samples and lock the assumption.

Best,
Marissa
